body:
> We need a more common method for letting user have a bit more freedom on the markup generated.

We do not have a way to do this right now. And the solution to this ultimately is full blown templates with events like `<ul><li onClick..`.
I don't want to go too far in the "control the generated DOM" beside adding css classes mostly because I cannot right now think of use cases where it really makes sense.

> I'm pretty sure I will need a lot more html attributes in the future

If we cannot think of any use case right now I would prefer to stick with something simpler and see in the future if we need more than that. We will have more use cases and experiences of using the instantsearch.js.

I'd rather solve the `label + select` use case by adding an id rather than add an API that the user **might** use. So that we can keep the `rootClass` `itemClass`. Instead of itemHtmlAttributes, rootHtmlAttributes etc..

> htmlAttributes might not be the right choice, though. It is a Javascript object, and some keys (like class and for) will have to be renamed (as cssClass and htmlFor) before being actually passed to React.

And we do not know what are the other possible keys that will need to be renamed because attributes here are somehow managed by react.
